supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to cmupdate.exe running from Ben Carter's AppData directory, and the proxy records show connections to update.chartmate-imaging.net at roughly five-minute intervals. The inventory instead identifies the approved updater as C:\Program Files\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe and its update host as update.chartmate-imaging.com.

The AppData cmupdate.exe created a file at its own path and a temporary MSI file during the observed update activity; the records do not establish that these files are legitimate ChartMate components.
Google Drive File Stream, a cloud-storage service not listed as approved, started on the workstation.
Chrome accessed the AWS console and its console assets; AWS access is not identified in the approved-services context.
GlobalProtect's PanGPS process started on the workstation, despite the inventory context stating there is no VPN.

A Meridian OpsAgent process ran as SYSTEM and generated an explicit-credentials event targeting svc-bkp on DC-HD-01. The supplied records do not show whether that credential attempt succeeded; the agent is not identified in the approved-services context.

A UserAssist registry value decodes from ROT13 to a reference to C:\Windows\System32\mstsc.exe, indicating use of Remote Desktop Connection on this workstation; the context says remote administration is only done from WS-OHADDAD-01.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS destinations and some inspected requests, but do not provide the contents of the periodic ChartMate-host traffic.
No executable hashes, file signatures, or software-installation provenance are provided for the AppData cmupdate.exe, Meridian OpsAgent, or GlobalProtect.
The supplied records do not confirm that the svc-bkp credential attempt succeeded.
The evidence covers only the specified time window and does not establish the activity's full history or outcomes.
claims_not_established: That the AppData cmupdate.exe is definitively malware or that its traffic exfiltrated data.
That Google Drive File Stream or AWS access involved a personal account, data transfer, or unauthorized data access.
That the svc-bkp credential attempt succeeded or that the account was compromised.
That the GlobalProtect process established a VPN connection or that mstsc.exe established a remote session.
Who initiated or authorized the anomalous software and service activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze the AppData cmupdate.exe and MSI temporary file, including hashes, signatures, download origin, and endpoint security detections.
Obtain proxy and endpoint process telemetry for all connections from the AppData cmupdate.exe, including any available TLS inspection details and related DNS records.
Review DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 authentication and security logs for successful svc-bkp authentication or subsequent use from WS-BCARTER-01.
Determine the provenance, installation time, configuration, and network activity of Meridian OpsAgent and GlobalProtect on WS-BCARTER-01.
Review browser and cloud audit records for AWS and Google Drive access, including account identity and any file activity.
Check endpoint telemetry for mstsc.exe execution and any resulting remote connections.
